s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms started in childhood
Night blindness is the only symptom reported
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision is normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
ERG shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Rod electroretinogram is flat
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
Marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms started in childhood
Night blindness is the only symptom reported
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision is normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
ERG shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Rod electroretinogram is flat
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
Marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and progressive loss of retinal function as indicated by electroretinogram (ERG) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) findings are consistent with rod-cone dystrophy. The presence of supernormal thickness in the perifoveal region and marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas on OCT also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: While retinitis pigmentosa could explain night blindness, the lack of significant pigmentary degeneration on fundus examination and the specific pattern of retinal thickening on OCT make rod-cone dystrophy a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Congenital stationary night blindness
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by night blindness without progressive vision loss, which contradicts the patient's progressive ERG changes and OCT findings indicating retinal degeneration.

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with severe visual impairment or blindness in early childhood, which does not match the patient's relatively preserved visual acuity and late presentation.

rejected.label: Autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: While this could be a consideration, the specific findings of supernormal perifoveal thickness and the pattern of retinal degeneration on OCT are more characteristic of rod-cone dystrophy.
